title: Rare-Earth Nickelate Single Crystals at the Atomic-Scale: From Infinite-Layer LaNiO2 to High-Pressure Superconductor La3Ni2O7
content: Rare-earth nickelates represent a versatile platform for exploring emergent quantum phases and advancing functional applications. The ability to precisely manipulate oxygen stoichiometry through topotactic transformations of perovskite nickelates has been instrumental in uncovering superconductivity in infinite-layer (IL) nickelate thin films [1]. However, understanding the atomic-scale mechanisms underpinning these phenomena remains critical [2, 3]. The recent discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in La3Ni2O7 at pressures exceeding 14 GPa has sparked significant research interest [4], yet the intrinsic properties of this phase remain under intense debate, particularly regarding its potential filamentary character.
